_about: Public-domain Daniel Denison Whedon (1808-1885), Methodist Episcopal theologian and editor of the Methodist Quarterly Review, for the Word Hoard: Public Addresses (1852), The Freedom of the Will (1864), What is Arminianism? (1879), Statements Theological and Critical (1887) Essays, Reviews and Discourses (1887) and, from round 57, his Commentary on the New Testament (5 vols, Hunt & Eaton printing; first issued 1860-1880), from Internet Archive scans. Added 2026-10-23 by lane A, round 52 (my pick); Adam may veto the whole shelf. Every printing dated before 1930, so public domain in the US. No uids minted.

whedon-public-addresses: Public addresses, collegiate and popular (Boston : J.P. Jewett, 1852)
whedon-freedom-of-will: The freedom of the will as a basis of human responsibility and a divine government : elucidated and maintained in its issue with the necessitarian theories of Hobbes, Edwards, the Princeton essayists, and other leading advocates (New York : Nelson & Phillips, 1864)
whedon-arminianism: What is Arminianism? : with a brief sketch of Arminius (Toronto : William Briggs, 1879)
whedon-statements: Statements, theological and critical (New York : Phillips & Hunt ; Cincinnati : Cranston & Stowe, 1887)
whedon-essays: Essays, reviews, and discourses (New York, Phillips & Hunt, 1887)
whedon-nt-1: Commentary on the New Testament, intended for popular use, vol. 1: Matthew and Mark (New York: Hunt & Eaton)
whedon-nt-2: Commentary on the New Testament, vol. 2: Luke and John (New York: Hunt & Eaton)
whedon-nt-3: Commentary on the New Testament, vol. 3: Acts and Romans (New York: Hunt & Eaton)
whedon-nt-4: Commentary on the New Testament, vol. 4: Corinthians to Second Timothy (New York: Hunt & Eaton)
whedon-nt-5: Commentary on the New Testament, vol. 5: Titus to Revelation (New York: Hunt & Eaton)

_alternates.whedon-nt-other-printings: Other printings of the same New Testament commentary: Carlton & Lanahan 1860-1880 volumes and the London Hodder & Stoughton 'Popular Commentary' (1874-1876)

_excluded.whedon-other: The Commentary on the Old Testament (1880s-1900s) he edited, whose volumes were written by other Methodist scholars; Letter to Dr. Stevens (1859, a pamphlet); Cox's Letters on the Second Coming (another author)
